name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility
headline: A globally important infrastructure for making biodiversity records discoverable across institutions and borders.
whatMakesPossible: Species occurrence context, source discovery, taxonomic reconciliation and source-aware Atlas observations.
datasets: GBIF Species API and Backbone Taxonomy
coverage: Global participant network with uneven coverage shaped by sampling effort, publishing capacity and digitisation history.
access: Public web and REST APIs; large occurrence extracts should use download services or snapshots rather than high-offset crawling.
licence: Occurrence datasets carry dataset-level Creative Commons licences. Dataset citation, attribution and licence metadata must remain attached to reused records.
freshness: Continuously indexed as publishers update; derived snapshots and taxonomy versions change separately.
limitations: GBIF is an index and access infrastructure, not the original observer or owner of every record.
Occurrence records do not establish complete range, abundance, population trend or live tracking.
No records does not prove species absence.
sensitiveData: Publishers may withhold or generalise sensitive information; downstream use must preserve those restrictions.

name: International Union for Conservation of Nature
headline: A global conservation union and expert network producing recognised assessments, standards and guidance.
whatMakesPossible: Species-status context, conservation standards, risk semantics and expert knowledge that can be connected to claim-level evidence.
datasets: IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
coverage: Global assessment and membership remit; individual species, place and programme coverage must be established separately.
access: Public web access; Red List API v4 requires a token and is subject to purpose and rate-limit controls.
licence: Red List API access is non-commercial under its API terms; commercial routes require separate licensing. Full citation remains required.
freshness: Red List releases occur multiple times per year; assessment dates remain species-specific.
limitations: IUCN authority does not replace claim-level evidence.
A global remit does not prove programme activity in every geography.
Assessment category is not a live measurement of a population at every place.
sensitiveData: Some spatial and threat details may be restricted or generalised.

name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System
headline: A global IOC-UNESCO network making marine biodiversity occurrence and event data easier to discover and reuse responsibly.
whatMakesPossible: Marine occurrence context, ocean biodiversity discovery, source-aware Atlas records and relationships between datasets, nodes and taxonomic authorities.
coverage: Global ocean with uneven sampling and provider coverage.
access: Public API, mapper, downloads and analysis tooling; large analyses should prefer documented exports.
licence: Underlying datasets may use CC0, CC BY or CC BY-NC. Dataset citations and licences must remain visible in downstream reuse.
freshness: Continuously harvested with periodic integrated exports and delayed-mode updates.
limitations: OBIS integrates and enriches records but is not the original observer for most data.
Occurrence density is not abundance.
No marine record does not establish absence.
sensitiveData: OBIS policy supports restriction or generalisation for species, habitats, confidentiality and Indigenous data concerns and explicitly references FAIR and CARE principles.

name: Catalogue of Life
headline: A global taxonomic checklist infrastructure connecting expert sources into versioned species-name releases.
whatMakesPossible: Taxon reconciliation, source identity, versioned taxonomy and clearer provenance for species profiles.
coverage: Global taxonomic names with documented incompleteness and revision over time.
access: Public web access, downloads and ChecklistBank machine access; some custom operations may require authentication.
licence: Catalogue and source conditions must be preserved at the relevant release and source level; underlying source terms can differ.
limitations: A checklist is not an occurrence database.
A checklist is not a range map or conservation assessment.
Absence from a checklist does not prove a taxon is invalid or nonexistent.
sensitiveData: Taxonomic names are generally non-sensitive; linked occurrence or distribution records can have separate restrictions.

name: World Register of Marine Species
headline: An expert-managed marine taxonomic reference connecting accepted names, synonyms and stable Aphia identifiers.
whatMakesPossible: Marine taxon reconciliation, source-aware species identity and a stronger taxonomic bridge between OBIS records and 4PLANET Species.
coverage: Global marine taxonomy; completeness and revision state vary across groups.
access: Public web and REST webservice for taxon matching and record retrieval.
licence: WoRMS citation and terms apply. Complete-database redistribution requires separate permission; source references remain material.
limitations: WoRMS is not a distribution database.
A taxonomic match is not abundance or conservation status.
Accepted taxonomic status can change with revision.
sensitiveData: Taxonomic records normally contain no sensitive occurrence geography; linked occurrence data are separate entities.

name: NASA Earth Science Data Systems
headline: NASA infrastructure for discovering, archiving, processing and distributing Earth science observations and derived products.
whatMakesPossible: Source-aware Earth observation layers, environmental context and time-sensitive signals without collapsing processed products into direct field truth.
access: Earthdata Search, CMR API, cloud services and product-specific access; some downloads require Earthdata Login.
licence: NASA promotes open science and open data, but each product's documentation, attribution and third-party inputs must be checked before reuse.
freshness: Ranges from archive releases to near-real-time products.
limitations: Near-real-time is not live.
Processed satellite products are not direct field truth.
Cloud screening, algorithm version, level and spatial resolution materially affect interpretation.
sensitiveData: Most Earth-observation products are open; ancillary or third-party inputs may carry separate terms.

name: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem
headline: European infrastructure for accessing Sentinel and other Copernicus Earth observation data and processing services.
whatMakesPossible: Source-aware imagery and environmental context for land, ocean, atmosphere and place monitoring.
coverage: Global for many Sentinel missions, product dependent.
access: Documented STAC, OData, openEO and other services; authentication varies by service.
licence: Copernicus data are generally provided under free, full and open access terms with attribution and product-specific conditions.
freshness: Mission and processing dependent, with frequent acquisition and reprocessing.
limitations: The Data Space is an access platform, not the original institution behind every derived product.
No image or clear pixel does not prove absence of an ecological feature.
Sensor, cloud and processing limits must remain visible.
sensitiveData: Most products are open; security-sensitive or third-party layers can differ.

name: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
actorTypeLabel: Public climate and ocean data archive
headline: A US public archive and stewardship centre for climate, ocean, coastal and geophysical information.
whatMakesPossible: Historic climate and ocean baselines, source-aware environmental context and validation of time-sensitive signals.
coverage: Global for major archives, with uneven station and source coverage.
access: Climate Data Online API and dataset-specific web, download and machine-access services.
licence: Many US federal data are public domain, while international contributions and product-specific terms still require source-level review and citation.
freshness: Dataset-specific, from daily feeds to periodic releases.
limitations: NCEI hosts many distinct datasets; no single licence or method describes all holdings.
No station or record does not prove no event or condition occurred.
Reconstructions and interpolations must remain distinct from direct observations.
sensitiveData: Generally open, with source- or operationally specific restrictions possible.

name: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
headline: An intergovernmental assessment platform synthesising scientific, Indigenous and local knowledge for policy.
whatMakesPossible: High-level evidence synthesis, issue context and decision support with explicit confidence and knowledge-system boundaries.
coverage: Global and regional depending on assessment scope.
access: Primarily publication, catalogue and repository access; there is no single universal raw-data API for all assessment evidence.
licence: Publication and supporting-data terms vary by assessment and underlying source.
freshness: Assessment-cycle based rather than live or near-real-time.
limitations: IPBES assessments are syntheses, not raw observations.
Institutional authority does not replace claim-level evidence.
A topic not addressed by an assessment is not evidence of absence or irrelevance.
sensitiveData: IPBES knowledge and data policy recognises FAIR and CARE principles and requires respect for Indigenous and local knowledge systems.

name: Global Forest Watch
headline: A WRI-led forest monitoring platform combining satellite products, alerts and contextual datasets.
whatMakesPossible: Forest-pressure context, source-aware change signals and easier exploration of land-cover information across providers.
datasets: Global Forest Watch Integrated Deforestation Alerts
access: Web, downloads and APIs vary by individual layer and service.
licence: Each layer retains provider-specific licence and attribution; platform access does not unify all rights.
freshness: Ranges from near-real-time alerts to annual products.
limitations: Alerts are potential change signals and require validation.
Tree-cover loss is not automatically deforestation.
Platform layers must retain original provider, method, date and licence.
sensitiveData: Some local contextual layers can have separate restrictions.

name: MapBiomas
headline: A collaborative network producing annual land-cover, land-use and thematic map collections with strong regional expertise.
whatMakesPossible: Long-term land-cover context and regionally informed analysis of forests, water, fire and land-use change.
coverage: Strong Latin American coverage with an expanding network of regional initiatives.
access: Web and downloads; machine access varies by collection and platform.
licence: MapBiomas attribution and collection-specific terms apply; underlying imagery can have separate conditions.
limitations: Classified pixels are model outputs, not direct field observations.
Accuracy varies by class, geography, year and collection version.
An unchanged class does not prove no local ecological change.
sensitiveData: Generally open thematic mapping; source and local-data restrictions must still be respected.

name: Artsdatabanken
headline: Norway's public knowledge centre for species, habitats, occurrence records, Red Lists and alien-species assessments.
whatMakesPossible: A stronger Norwegian Species and Place layer, taxonomic and assessment context and a future source graph for Oslofjord and national biodiversity data.
coverage: Norway and relevant Norwegian territories, product dependent.
access: Multiple public web services and APIs; product-specific documentation and source licences apply.
licence: Norwegian public-data licences and source-record terms vary by product and must be checked before integration.
freshness: Occurrence services update continuously while assessment lists follow defined release cycles.
limitations: Artsdatabanken is not the original observer for every occurrence record.
No record in Artskart does not prove species absence.
A Red List category is an assessment, not a live sensor.
sensitiveData: Sensitive species locations may be generalised or withheld.
